cards.text: Paul, the apostle, is writing a letter to the church in Corinth. He just asked them whether they want him to come with a rod, or in love and with a gentle spirit (1 Corinthians 4:21). Now he turns to a report about them: there's sexual immorality among them, and a man has his father's wife.

cards.question: Paul says this kind of sexual immorality isn't tolerated even among ___.
With this going on among them, how does Paul say the Corinthians are acting?

cards.text: Paul says they should have been stricken with grief instead. That's like the smoke alarm SCREAMING and everybody in the kitchen standing around bragging about how good the place smells.

cards.question: Paul says the church should have removed the man who did this from their ___.

cards.text: Paul isn't in Corinth. He's absent from them in body, but he says he's present with them in spirit.

cards.question: Paul says he'll wait until he gets to Corinth to pronounce judgment on the man who did this.

cards.text: When they're assembled in the name of the Lord Jesus, with Paul there in spirit and the power of the Lord Jesus, they're to hand this man over to Satan for the destruction of the flesh. That's heavy, friend. But Paul gives a reason.

cards.question: Paul says the man is handed over to Satan for a reason. What does Paul want for the man's spirit on the Day of the Lord?

cards.text: Paul tells them their boasting is not good. Then he pulls an example straight out of the KITCHEN, and friend, I just hopped so high my gold base left the ground.

cards.question: Paul says a little leaven works through the whole batch of dough.

cards.text: So Paul says to get rid of the old leaven, so they can be a new unleavened batch, as they really are. I'm not crying, friend. That's just flour in my eyebrows.

cards.question: Paul says Christ has been sacrificed. Which feast's lamb does Paul call Christ?

cards.text: So Paul says let's keep the feast. But not with the old bread, leavened with malice and wickedness.

cards.question: Instead of old bread leavened with malice and wickedness, what does Paul say to keep the feast with?

answers.text: The unleavened bread of sincerity and of truth
The unleavened bread of patience and of peace
The unleavened bread of joy and of kindness

cards.text: Next, Paul brings up an earlier letter where he told the Corinthians not to associate with sexually immoral people. Now he spells out what he meant.

cards.question: Paul meant the Corinthians should stay away from every sexually immoral person in the world.

cards.text: Paul says he wasn't including the sexually immoral, the greedy, swindlers or idolaters of this world, or they'd have to leave this world. Friend, I've got a whole planet to myself, and it is just big enough for ONE bakery and ONE very proud mustache.

cards.question: So who does Paul tell the Corinthians not to associate with?

answers.text: Anyone who claims to be a brother but lives that way
Anyone who doesn't belong to their church
Anyone who lives outside the city of Corinth

cards.text: Paul names what he means: someone who's sexually immoral or greedy, an idolater or a verbal abuser, a drunkard or a swindler.

cards.question: Paul says that with someone who claims to be a brother but lives like this, do not even ___ with him.

cards.text: Then Paul asks what business it is of his to judge those outside the church, and whether the Corinthians aren't to judge those inside.

cards.question: Paul says God will judge those outside the church.
Paul ends with a command for the church about the wicked man. What is it?

answers.text: Pray for him day and night
Send him to Paul at once

findings.problem: The question opens with "With this going on among them," and "this" points back to the immorality described on card 1, which is no longer on screen. The question should say what is going on, for example a man having his father's wife.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The story card has three sentences: the old leaven line, "I'm not crying, friend." and "That's just flour in my eyebrows."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The crying joke has no action in common with the fact, which is getting rid of the old leaven so the batch is new. Nothing in the moment explains why he'd be moved to tears, so a stranger would say "huh?" Being sentimental also fits poorly in a passage about church discipline.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The three answers differ only in which virtues complete the phrase: "sincerity and of truth" versus "patience and of peace" versus "joy and of kindness." Each wrong pair contrasts with malice and wickedness just as well, so the baker can only guess the wording. Nothing on the earlier cards lets the baker reason to the answer.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: The joke doesn't land. Paul's point is that avoiding every immoral person would mean leaving the world. The punchline is that his planet only has room for one bakery and one mustache, and that doesn't connect to the point without explaining. It also clashes with the backstory, where he invites bakers to come help him there.

rule.text: If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.

findings.problem: The right answer, "Anyone who claims to be a brother but lives that way," uses "that way" to point back to the list on card 3, which isn't on screen. That list (5:10) also doesn't match 5:11, which adds verbal abusers and drunkards.
